newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields rise despite CPI fall.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields rise despite CPI fall.

text.p: Swedish bond yields rose higher as the crown weakened, on market talk that the central bank would be compelled to raise rates to protect the currency.

A fall in February consumer prices rather than an expected rise only managed to push back yields temporarily. The CPI decreased by 0.1 percent month-on-month whereas expectations were for an increase of 0.2 percent. The year-on-year fall was 0.4 percent.
But the market focus, dealers say, is on the crown rather than on inflation. "Riksbank governor Urban Backstrom has said that inflation is not a problem", one dealer said.
Moreover, the central bank has said that the crown is too weak for rate cuts.
Statistics Sweden will publish fourth-quarter 1996 GDP data at 12.00 GMT. The market expects a rise of 1.7 percent from the third quarter.
* Six month T-bill rises one basis point to 4.28 pct.
* Ten year bond yield up two basis point higher to 6.88 pct.
* Crown softens to 4.4960 to mark vs 4.4710 late on Tuesday
